summary.headline: Hyundai Motor India Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 9.3% from 13.3% on a supplier fire, export disruption and commodity costs; FY27 guidance kept.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 total sales fell 1.3% YoY to 1,78,082 units, with domestic volumes up 5.4% to 1,39,374 and exports down to 38,708 from 48,140. A June supplier fire and the West Asia conflict hit volumes, and revenue was flat at INR 163,346 million. EBITDA fell 31% YoY to INR 15,117 million, with margin at 9.3% versus 13.3%, and PAT fell 35% to INR 8,886 million. Management kept FY27 domestic volume growth guidance of 8-10% and EBITDA margin guidance of 11-14%, and said the lost June production is almost fully recovered in July.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Sales of 1,39,374 units, up 5.4% YoY; SUVs were 70% of mix. Rural share rose to 25.9-26% and rural volume grew 23.2% while urban grew 2.8%. Venue posted its highest-ever quarterly volume; Aura and Exter hit record CNG shares of 95% and 32%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Volume fell to 38,708 units from 48,140 on West Asia disruption and June production loss. Central and South America grew 23% YoY. Export ASP rose about 7% YoY and 5-6% QoQ, helped by a mix shift to hatchbacks for CSA. SUVs were only 13-14% of exports.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic volume growth guidance of 8-10% reiterated; management says H2 must grow at least 8-10% after 5.4% in Q1.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11-14% reiterated, with pricing actions taken as needed to stay in range.
June production loss of about 13,900 units (mostly Creta) expected to be fully recovered in Q2, with most done in July.
Export volumes expected to recover from Q2 onwards; management expects Q2+ quarters to beat 48,000 units.
Pune third shift from October 2026 brings the 170,000-unit Phase 1 capacity to three-shift operation, about two years ahead of plan.
Industry growth in H2 FY27 seen in low single digits after the GST base effect; full-year industry growth guessed at 6-9%.
capex_capacity: Pune Phase 1 capacity of 170,000 units moves to three-shift operation from October 2026; Pune output is Venue for domestic and export.
Chennai Plant 1 utilisation is about 72% in CY2026 and is expected to reach about 88-92% in CY2027 as new models ramp.
New ICE mid-SUV launch planned for the festive season; a dedicated mass-market EV is planned with PLI eligibility targeted from day 1.
Localisation is 83%, up from about 77-78% a couple of years ago; target 90% by 2030.
Production disruption in June cost about 13,900 units, mostly Creta; recovery is mostly done in July.
demand_pricing: Commodity cost impact was about 100 bps QoQ and about 200 bps YoY, mainly precious metals and copper.
Three price hikes totalling about 100 bps have been taken so far in calendar 2026; further hikes will be calibrated.
Sequential margin hit came from higher discounts and lower seasonal government incentives; discounts are still below industry average.
Dealer inventory fell in June; management plans to rebuild inventory in July-September for the festive season without overloading dealers.
Freight costs rose, mainly on exports, but are generally passed on to distributors.
Employee cost rose about 20% YoY, mainly from Pune plant commencement and salary revisions.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity pressure was absorbed in Q1, and will more price hikes come?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodities cost about 100 bps QoQ and 200 bps YoY; mitigated by calibrated pricing, cost reduction and one-offs from Q4. Three price hikes (about 100 bps) so far in calendar 2026, with future hikes depending on commodity trends.

qa_highlights.question: Is Hyundai still comfortable with the 11-14% margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is not 'comfortable' but will take pricing or volume actions as needed to stay within 11-14%. It expects raw material costs to ease in coming months and will keep discounts in check.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Chennai Plant 1 utilisation and Pune third shift lift volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant 1 Chennai is at about 72% in CY2026, expected to reach about 90-92% in CY2027. The Pune third shift adds potential capacity of 170,000 units from October 2026, which management will ramp as demand allows.

qa_highlights.question: What are the export drivers and ASP outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are the new Venue (29 markets now, targeting 35), Exter LHD (13 markets by Q3) and Verna PE (25+ markets by Q3). ASP is helped by the hatch-heavy CSA mix; Middle East automatic models should lift ASP when that market reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Is rural demand slowing, and are there concerns about El Nino?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no rural slowdown: rural volume grew 23.2% YoY and rural share rose to 25.9% from 22.6%. Six of every ten new outlets are rural.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the industry and Hyundai's exit market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 industry growth in the low single digits and full-year industry growth of about 6-9%. FY26 exit share was about 12.3%, and management expects to exit FY27 above that level with two new models.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on commodity prices (copper, precious metals) and pricing actions, and management admits the outlook is uncertain.
Export recovery depends on West Asia shipping and freight disruption, including the Strait of Hormuz, and on the Mexico tariff situation.
H2 needs at least 8-10% growth against a higher GST-era base, and industry growth may slow to low single digits from October.
Launch timing and reception of the festive-season mid-SUV and dedicated EV, including PLI approval, which management says is subject to administrative timing.
Creta FMC timing was not disclosed; management said it will announce at the right time.
Employee cost growth (about 20% YoY) and the cost of ramping Pune capacity may keep pressure on margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on recovery and guidance, but cautious on margins: management repeatedly said it is not 'comfortable' with commodity costs and will act on pricing and volume to stay within the 11-14% EBITDA range. It was specific on the June disruption being fully recovered and on the H2 levers (two new models, Pune third shift, fleet sales).
key_quotes: Comfortable is not the word. Nobody can be comfortable in this kind of a scenario.
we expect to recover the impacted production volume within Q2 with most of it having already been recovered in July month itself.
we remain confident of delivering EBITDA margin within our guided range of 11% - 14% for FY27.
we are progressing with preparations to commence third-shift operations at our Pune facility from October 2026.

adds.what: Pune Phase 1 170,000-unit plant moves to three-shift operation (capacity uplift via third shift)

growth.why: FY27 domestic volume growth of 8-10% and EBITDA margin of 11-14% reiterated; Pune third shift from October 2026 adds capacity on the 170,000-unit Phase 1 line and Chennai utilisation is guided to rise from 72% to 88-90% in CY2027, but the 8-10% H2 domestic growth needed after 5.4% in Q1 is only partly backed by specific numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 9.3% from 13.3% YoY, below the 11-14% FY27 guide, with commodity costs up about 200 bps YoY; three price hikes (~100 bps) taken so far, and management says it is 'not comfortable' and will price or cut volume to stay in range.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pune Phase 1 170,000-unit capacity moves to three-shift operation from October 2026, about two years ahead of plan, with work already under way.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic volume guided at 8-10% for FY27 after 5.4% in Q1, so H2 needs at least 8-10%; Q2+ exports are expected to beat 48,000 units vs 38,708 in Q1, and June production loss of ~13,900 units is almost fully recovered in July.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Chennai Plant 1 utilisation is about 72% and guided to 88-92% in CY2027 as new models ramp, so there is no urgent new plant need yet; a dedicated mass-market EV is planned but no capex amount or date was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was only held, not raised; management is not 'comfortable' with the 11-14% margin range and Q1 domestic growth was only 5.4% against 8-10% needed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin of 9.3% sits below the 11-14% range, H2 needs 8-10% domestic growth against a GST-era base, and industry growth may slow to low single digits from October.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A new ICE mid-SUV is planned for the festive season, and two new models are cited for H2 with Exter LHD (13 markets by Q3) and Verna PE (25+ markets by Q3) export rollouts.

rows.label: Further price hikes to defend 11-14% margin
rows.why: Three hikes (~100 bps) taken in CY2026 so far; management says further hikes will be calibrated to commodity trends and commodities cost ~200 bps YoY.

rows.label: Export recovery from West Asia reopening and new models
rows.why: Management expects Q2+ export volumes above 48,000 units vs 38,708 in Q1; Venue is in 29 markets targeting 35, and Middle East automatic models should lift ASP when that market reopens.

rows.label: Mass-market EV with PLI eligibility from day 1
rows.why: A dedicated mass-market EV is planned with PLI eligibility targeted from day 1, but approval is subject to administrative timing and no launch date was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on June-disruption recovery, FY27 guidance and H2 levers (Pune third shift, two new models, fleet sales), but cautious on commodity-driven margins, which it said it was not 'comfortable' with; analysts pushed on margin defence, pricing and the H2 volume needed.
